events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The dispute is a $6.61 cancellation fee on a completed-booking cancellation, so it can only enter the policy through NS-0, which branches on `cancelled_by`: rider → NS-4, driver declaring a no-show → NS-1/NS-2, driver cancelling for another reason → NS-3. The record has `cancelled_by = None` [F4], so the branch cannot be selected and neither NS-1 nor NS-4 can be applied to this fee [NS-0]. [F7] merely confirms the $6.61 was charged; it does not identify the cancelling party.

The underlying facts are also internally inconsistent. One timeline says the platform recorded driver arrival at 17:27:05 and the cancellation came 5 min 40 s later [F5], while the driver's own "I'm Here" tap is recorded at 17:28:05, 42 m from the pickup, with the driver staying within 200 m for only 4 min 40 s after that tap [F6]. NS-1 requires the tap, the GPS position at the tap within the pickup radius, and then a continuous wait of more than 3 minutes until cancellation; on the tap-based timeline the in-radius wait is 4 min 40 s (> 180 s) and the position is 42 m [F6][NS-1], but the trace settles neither who cancelled nor that the wait ran continuously to the cancellation moment, and the driver's written statement asserting he waited and the rider never boarded is only a statement, not a system record [F11]. The chat contains a single timestamped message from the driver announcing arrival [F9][F10]; the rider sent nothing and there is no rider message at all.

No amount can be computed because RD-2's per-kilometre distance formula does not apply to this RydeX fixed-quote fare and no unexempt segment exists; the only sum in play is the $6.61 fee [F7], whose disposition depends on the missing `cancelled_by` value [NS-0]. Profile facts (rider 0 disputes/0 upheld [F15]; driver 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 d [F16]) cannot decide the case and, since no violation is established here, they do not support an account flag [RD-6]. Traffic and weather records [F12][F13][F14] are irrelevant to a no-show fee. With the decisive record missing, the trace's only permitted outcome is escalation, so I escalate rather than treat the gap as favouring either side.
